page.text: Poitiers.net – Le guide passionné de Poitiers Aller au contenu Rechercher: Accueil La Ville Actualité Infos Pratiques Annuaire Accueil La Ville Actualité Infos Pratiques Annuaire Poitiers.net : le guide passionné de Poitiers Poitiers.net : le guide passionné de Poitiers La ville de Poitiers vue par ses habitants Bienvenue sur Poitiers.net , un site créé par des Pictaviens passionnés pour partager l’amour de Poitiers . Histoire, patrimoine, vie locale et conseils pratiques : tout pour mieux connaître et apprécier cette ville unique. La ville Découvrir Actualités Découvrir Guide pratique et local Retrouvez des informations utiles, des événements, des lieux emblématiques et un annuaire de professionnels à Poitiers . Poitiers.net est authentique, local et conçu par ceux qui vivent Poitiers au quotidien. Pratiques Découvrir Entreprises Découvrir Découvrez Poitiers avec des Pictaviens Poitiers.net est conçu par des habitants de Poitiers, pour tous ceux qui souhaitent découvrir la ville de Poitiers , son patrimoine unique et sa vie locale. Notre objectif est de partager notre passion pour Poitiers à travers des articles clairs et pratiques, rédigés par ceux qui connaissent la ville au quotidien. Histoire et patrimoine de Poitiers Plongez dans l’histoire millénaire de Poitiers , ses monuments emblématiques, ses ruelles chargées d’histoire et son architecture remarquable. Que vous souhaitiez visiter Poitiers , en apprendre plus sur son passé ou explorer la ville autrement, nos contenus vous offrent un regard local et authentique. Informations pratiques et vie locale Retrouvez des informations pratiques pour mieux profiter de la ville : événements locaux, services municipaux, transports et conseils pour découvrir Poitiers comme un Pictavien. Notre approche n’est pas exhaustive, mais elle est guidée par l’amour et la connaissance de la ville. Annuaire des professionnels de Poitiers Nous proposons également un annuaire de professionnels à Poitiers , sélectionnés pour leur sérieux et leur expertise. Que vous recherchiez un artisan, un commerçant ou un prestataire de services, Poitiers.net vous guide vers des acteurs locaux fiables, afin de soutenir l’économie de la ville. Un site pour partager notre passion de Poitiers Poitiers.net n’a pas pour but d’être un guide complet ou institutionnel. Il s’agit d’un site créé par des Pictaviens , pour partager l’amour de Poitiers, ses richesses et son dynamisme. Découvrez Poitiers à travers nos yeux, nos conseils et nos coups de cœur, pour vivre pleinement cette ville unique. page.title: La Rochelle: Things to Do, Harbour Walks and Island Trips
page.text: La Rochelle: Things to Do, Harbour Walks and Island Trips Skip navigation La-Rochelle.org Tours Boat trips Walking tours Île de Ré Getting there DE Find a tour Your independent La Rochelle guide La Rochelle : Boat Trips, City Walks and Atlantic Islands La Rochelle brings harbour towers, an aquarium and Atlantic boat trips together. Start with the Old Port on a short visit, or give a separate day to the coast and islands. Compare La Rochelle tours → See tours on this page ↓ ★ Boat trips and city tours compared ⚓ Old Port walks and island crossings ↺ Check free cancellation by tour La Rochelle sights at a glance La Rochelle is a port city in Charente-Maritime on France’s Atlantic coast. For a short visit, start at the Vieux-Port, where the harbour towers mark the entrance, and use the Grosse Horloge as your landmark on the way into the old town. If the sea is the reason you came, keep time for a beach, a sail or a separate island trip. La Concurrence is the city-centre beach. Les Minimes and Chef de Baie give you other stretches of coast to aim for. Choose the harbour and old town walk for the towers and the story of the wine and salt trade, or compare private tours if the visit is for your own group. Vieux-Port Harbour towers and the Grosse Horloge city gate About 5 minutes on foot From La Rochelle station to the aquarium Île de Ré Bridge crossing from La Rochelle to Rivedoux-Plage La Rochelle tours Choose a food walk with a local guide for a taste of the city, or a guided walk if you prefer its streets. For time on the water, compare the narrated cruise and catamaran sails. Hand-picked tours, booked through GetYourGuide. Prices are indicative starting prices in euros (as of November 2026). Tap a tour for live availability and the current price in your currency. Tickets to other attractions are extra. Check availability → Sailing from €46 Catamaran sailing towards Fort Boyard 🕒 4 hours 📍 15 Avenue Michel Crépeau, La Rochelle ⭐ 4.8 (709 reviews) Captain and crew Water Security equipment Sail from La Rochelle towards Fort Boyard. Entry is not included. From March 2026 to spring 2028, boats must stay at least 480 m from Fort Boyard. Check availability → Guided walk from €40 Guided walk through La Rochelle 🕒 2 hours 📍 Place de la Chaîne, La Rochelle ⭐ 4.9 (98 reviews) Guide This public walk starts at Place de la Chaîne. Tower admission is extra. Check availability → Coastal sail from €29 Daytime coastal sail from La Rochelle 🕒 2 hours 📍 15 Avenue Michel Crépeau, La Rochelle ⭐ 4.7 (264 reviews) Water Safety equipment A daytime sail along the coast from La Rochelle. Check availability → Sea cruise from €23 Commented cruise towards Fort Boyard 🕒 130 minutes 📍 Cours des Dames, ticket office 1, La Rochelle ⭐ 4.7 (1,672 reviews) Narrated sea cruise The route offers views of Île d’Aix without a landing. Entry to Fort Boyard is not included. From March 2026 to spring 2028, boats must stay at least 480 m from Fort Boyard. Check availability → Guided walks and boat trips in La Rochelle Compare a food walk with a local guide, a harbour history tour from Place de la Chaîne and sailings along the coast or towards Fort Boyard. Browse all tours on GetYourGuide → Aquarium La Rochelle on Quai Louis Prunier Aquarium La Rochelle is about five minutes on foot from the railway station, and a visit takes about 1.5 to 2 hours. An aquarium ticket with a timed slot guarantees entry at the booked time and is recommended when you are fitting the aquarium around a train or a sailing. Plan the aquarium as a visit in its own right. As of November 2026, admission is €18.50 for adults, €14.50 for ages 13 to 17 and €12.50 for ages 3 to 12. Children under 3 enter free. Children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult, and pushchairs and wheelchairs are allowed. From 2 November to 18 December 2026, the aquarium opens from 10:00 to 19:00, with last entry at 17:30. Keep meals outside the exhibition route and switch off the flash if you take photographs. Once you leave, the visit is over, so allow time to go through the displays at your own pace before heading back towards the harbour. La Rochelle’s coast, Fort Boyard and the islands La Rochelle has coastal sails for time on the water, Fort Boyard cruises for a view of the sea fort and a separate boat excursion for time ashore on Île d’Aix. The narrated Fort Boyard cruise from the Old Port sails past Île d’Aix without landing. For time on the island itself, use the dedicated Aix trip from Cours des Dames and plan around the return sailing. Île de Ré is reached by bridge. Start with the crossing to Île de Ré if you want to spend your time in island villages, on the coast or near the salt landscapes. The boat trip guide explains the Fort Boyard navigation zone and the steps at the Aix landing. For a city day with a food focus, the guided walk from Quai Duperré explores local flavours with a local guide. Plan a visit to La Rochelle La Rochelle works as a base for harbour walks, coast trips and a bridge crossing to Île de Ré. Choose a guide for the part of the visit you want to organise first. Tours La Rochelle tours Compare food walks, a narrated cruise and guided cycling. Boats Fort Boyard and boat trips Compare coastal sailing, Fort Boyard routes and the separate trip ashore on Aix. History Old Port and old town walks Follow the towers, the city gate and the streets behind the harbour. Private tours Private walks and sailing Compare private city walks with a catamaran for your group. Transport Getting to La Rochelle Plan arrival by train, airport bus or car. Areas Where to stay Choose an area by the walks and connections you will use. Seasons When to visit Compare monthly weather, beach supervision and boat timetables. Island Île de Ré Cross by bridge and choose between villages, beaches and salt landscapes. La Rochelle visitor questions La Rochelle’s Old Port is a practical starting point for the city and its boat trips, while the aquarium and Île de Ré each have their own visit arrangements. What should I see first in La Rochelle? La Rochelle’s Old Port is the place to begin if time is limited. Look towards the harbour entrance to see the towers, then walk through the Grosse Horloge into the streets of the old town. If the coast is your priority, continue your day at La Concurrence. How long does Aquarium La Rochelle take? About 1.5 to 2 hours is a useful allowance for Aquarium La Rochelle. Start from Quai Louis Prunier, about five minutes on foot from the station. A timed ticket guarantees your booked entry time, which is useful if you need to fit the visit around a train. Who publishes this La Rochelle guide? La-Rochelle.org is an independent guide, separate from the city’s tourist office and local tour operators. It brings together practical details for visiting the harbour, aquarium, beaches and nearby islands, alongside comparisons of guided outings and the travel arrangements you make for yourself.
